newsitem.title: USA: IPO SPOTLIGHT-Novel seen strong in debut.
newsitem.headline: IPO SPOTLIGHT-Novel seen strong in debut.

text.p: Novel Denim Holdings Ltd, the Hong Kong-based licensed maker of Gap and Wrangler jeans, is expected to make a strong showing on Wall Street when its shares make their trading debut Thursday.

Novel Denim increased its planned offering late Wednesday by 500,000 shares to 4.25 million, offering them in a price range of $15 and $17 each. The issue is to be priced after the market close Wednesday for trading on Nasdaq the next day.

The denim cloth and apparel manufacturer is controlled by Novel Apparel, which in turn is owned by Novel Enterprises Ltd of Hong Kong. The man heading it all is E.C. Silas Chou, a Hong Kong garment tycoon.

Chou is the chairman of the board of both Tommy Hilfiger and Pepe Jeans. Both companies are major purchasers of Novel Denim's garments, as is Gap Inc and VF Corp, the maker of Wrangler Jeans. VF is also buys raw denim cloth from Novel Denim.
Actual garment and fabric production takes place on the island nation of Mauritius, with a second facility being built on the island of Madagascar, both located off the southeast coast of Africa.

"The company has set itself up well," said Manish Shah, editor of the IPO Maven newsletter. "Their costs are based in the relatively weak local currency, while revenues are in European hard currencies and the labor costs are significantly lower than in the (European Union)."

The company's prospectus noted steady increases in sales, topping out in fiscal 1997 at $83.2 million. Most of Novel Denim's sales, 62 percent, are in the European Union (EU). Twenty-six percent are currently in Africa and nine percent in the United States. Net income during the same period was $11.1 million. Total assets were $66.7 million.
The company said it would use $7.7 million of IPO's net proceeds to pay off its long-term debt. The remaining short-term debt stands at $16.2 million.

Novel Denim is registered in the British Virgin Islands and benefits from the Lome Convention. The convention, made up of 15 EU nations and 70 African, Carribean and Pacific countries, allows Novel Denim to export its products to the EU free from duties and quotas.
Despite the beneficial trade agreement, the company requires more shipping time that its competitors, and its performance can be sensitive to the fluctuating price of cotton, it said.

One analyst made a warning of his own. "There is very little retail growth in Europe with a stagnant apparel market. However, Pepe Jeans is a big seller," noted Alan Millstein, the editor and publisher of the Fashion Network, an industry newsletter. "Quietly, this is a giant share offering."

But Kurt Barnard, editor and publisher of Barnard's Retail Marketing Report, said the products would sell despite a sluggish European economy and the high price for denim there compared with prices in the United States. "I don't care what the price is for denim. Most likely, they are less than other options for consumers."
The shares will trade on the Nasdaq under the symbol "NVLD." The total public offering represents roughly one third of the 13,187,500 common shares.
Of the total number of shares, 3.5 million will be sold in the United States and 750,000 shares will be sold in European markets by underwriters led by Morgan Stanley & Co Inc.
